finding.claim: The POST /hooks/test route fetches a callback URL taken from the request body, with no validation. Any caller can make the server send requests to internal hosts, such as cloud metadata at 169.254.169.254, localhost services and private networks. The response status is returned, which gives a blind-to-semi-blind oracle for probing internal ports and hosts.

trace.note: `pub` router is a public router; requireAdmin is not applied to it (only admin.use at line 12)
The value is passed directly to axios.post, which follows redirects by default and accepts any http/https URL
The upstream status code is returned to the caller

finding.guards_checked: No scheme, host or IP allowlist or denylist. No DNS resolution check. Redirects are not disabled. No authentication on the `pub` router in this file, and no auth middleware is visible here. If auth is applied where the router is mounted, that code is not in this directory, so it could not be checked.

verdict.reason: routes.js:19-21 passes req.body.callback straight to axios.post on the `pub` router, which has no requireAdmin (only `admin` uses it at line 12), with no URL validation, and returns the upstream status at line 21.

finding.claim: The GET /diagnostics/fetch route fetches an arbitrary URL from the query string with no destination validation. An admin, or anyone who has hijacked an admin session, can reach internal services and cloud metadata. The response status is returned. The only protection is the admin role check, so this is lower severity than ssrf-1.

trace.note: admin.use(requireAdmin) gates the router on session role === 'admin'
req.query.url is passed unchanged to axios.get, which follows redirects
The upstream status code is returned to the caller

finding.guards_checked: requireAdmin (routes.js:7-10) restricts the route to admin sessions. This is an authorization check, not an SSRF control. There is no scheme, host or IP validation and no redirect restriction. A query string value can also be an array (`?url=a&url=b`), which axios does not accept as a URL string. That is not a protection.

verdict.guard_found: requireAdmin (routes.js:7-10, applied at routes.js:12) is an admin-role gate only; there is no URL validation (no scheme, host or IP check)
verdict.reason: The trace is accurate (routes.js:12-16), and axios.get(req.query.url) at routes.js:15 has no URL validation, but the route sits behind admin.use(requireAdmin) at routes.js:12, which needs session.role === "admin", so an unauthenticated or low-privilege attacker cannot control the source.
